answer: Proof-of-Upkeep Registries. Each identity must publish a signed juniper-scented sensor reading from a physical device it operates, timestamped within a dawn window that rotates unpredictably. Peers cross-check readings against neighboring devices; a mismatch triggers a whisper review by three randomly drawn operators who re-sample. An attacker must run real hardware per identity and sustain daily calibration work, so cost scales with physical devices, not money.
